newsitem.title: USA: PSE&G seeks participation with reciprocity.
newsitem.headline: PSE&G seeks participation with reciprocity.

text.p: Marketing affiliates of out-of-state utilities should be permitted to participate in New Jersey's competitive marketplace, Public Service Electric & Gas Co President Lawrence Codey told regulators Tuesday.

In testimony prepared for the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities, he called for reciprocity -- for the ability of New Jersey utilities to sell power in areas served by the parents of the marketing companies selling in New Jersey.
"A truly competitive market will only be realized if competition exists over the entire range of the market," Cody said.

"If large utilities within feasible transmission range of Public Service (Enterprise Group Inc's utility subsidiary) operate in a closed maret environment and ship surplus power to Public Service retail customers directly or through affiliates, market distortions may well occur," he said.

Cody prposed that "if the parent utility's market is not open for competition within 12 months from the date that New Jersey open its markets, those affiliates would be required to relinquish their customers and cease participation" in New Jersey's market.
He told the board PSE&G proposed to open its entire system to competition effective January 1, 1999.
Monday Senior Vice President for Corporate Services Alfred Koeppe told reporters this is based on the expectation the board's final order will be issued "a little less than a year from now."
If it is delayed into October, he continued, the utility would have to delay its planned implementation.
Vice president of marketing Fritz Lark said the company expects to spend $10 million to educate its customers about the competitive market by the end of 1998.
